data.title: HackCelestial 3.0
data.details:
Note:

  • Only the Finalist / shortlisted teams will be required to pay a participation fee of ₹1,500.
  • You will receive the payment link only if you are shortlisted.
  • For the Problem Statements, please visit: https://tech.alegria.co.in/tracks

Overview:

HackCelestial is a high-energy, 24-hour innovation sprint that brings together talented student developers, designers, and problem-solvers to tackle real-world challenges. Participants are challenged to design and develop impactful solutions using Generative AI and core software development skills. Through intense collaboration, rapid prototyping, and creative thinking, teams compete to solve specific problem statements while pushing the boundaries of technology and innovation. Whether you're here to learn, build, or lead, HackCelestial offers the perfect platform to code, collaborate, and create something extraordinary.

  • Date: 26–27 September 2026
  • No. of Days: 2 Days
  • Members Count: 1–5 per team
  • Registration Fees: ₹1,500 per team (For Final Round) (Round 1, Idea Submission is FREE!)
  • Mode: Offline

Why HackCelestial 3.0:

  • Real World Problem Solving
  • Networking Opportunities
  • Mentor Guidance
  • Jamming Sessions
  • Exciting Goodies

Prize Pool: ₹1,50,000

  • Top 3 teams will receive cash prizes.
  • The top 5 teams will receive additional goodies as a special reward.
  • Award for Excellence in AI Application
  • Award for Excellence in User Interface Design

Theme: Hospitality & Travel

Calling all explorers, innovators, dreamers, and problem-solvers!

This HackCelestial, we’re taking innovation beyond the screen and into the world of hospitality and travel. It’s your chance to rethink how people explore new places, experience destinations, discover cultures, and connect with the world around them. From making travel more personalized and accessible to creating smarter hotel experiences and sustainable tourism solutions, there’s no limit to what you can build. Whether you’re passionate about travel, hospitality, technology, sustainability, or simply solving everyday problems, this is your opportunity to turn your ideas into something meaningful.

Bring your creativity, technical skills, and problem-solving mindset to the table as we work towards making travel more seamless, inclusive, memorable, and responsible.

Participants are encouraged to identify and develop solutions for real-world challenges across areas such as smart and personalized travel experiences, hospitality and guest experience, sustainable and responsible tourism, accessible and inclusive travel, local experiences and cultural discovery, and travel safety and convenience.

The goal is simple: reimagine travel, redefine hospitality, and build experiences that people will remember.

Facilities:

  • Free Accommodation (Accommodation within the campus)
  • Food Accessibility (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner)

Additional Perks:

  • Participation Certificate
  • Winner Certificate
  • Goodies

Rules & Guidelines:

  • Teams must consist of 1 to 5 members; cross-college teams are allowed.
  • Each team may submit only one problem statement solution, which must be original and developed during the hackathon.
  • Plagiarism or replication of existing solutions without significant modification will lead to immediate disqualification.
  • Submissions must be made through Unstop or Google Form, and all deadlines must be strictly followed; late submissions will not be evaluated.
  • A working prototype or simulation is mandatory for the finals.
  • Judges’ decisions are final and binding, and they may request technical clarifications or design justifications during evaluations.
  • Prize distribution for top-performing teams are subject to performance and interview rounds.
  • Teams must stay active and responsive regarding review schedules and shortlisting announcements.
  • All team members must bring their own devices and stay on campus for the full duration of the offline event; accommodation will be provided.
  • Participants are expected to maintain professionalism and discipline during all rounds and interactions.
  • Only official communications shared via the event website and email should be followed.
  • Teams violating rules or engaging in unethical practices will be disqualified immediately.

data.title: Inspiron 5.0
data.details:
The Computer Society of India (CSI) COEP Tech Student Chapter is excited to bring back Inspiron 5.0 with Simplify Healthcare as our Title Sponsor and Infotech.Works as our Co-Title Sponsor.

Get ready to put your skills to the test in this exciting fifth edition, where you'll tackle real-world challenges with innovative, cutting-edge solutions. This isn't just another hackathon-it’s a chance to work with the latest technologies, connect with industry pioneers, and expand your network. Whether you're here to compete, collaborate, or learn, Inspiron 5.0 promises an unforgettable experience.

Eligibility: Open to all UG, Diploma, and PG students.

Team Composition:

  • Teams must consist of 2 to 4 members
  • Inter-year teams: Allowed
  • Inter-branch team members: Allowed
  • Inter-college team members: Allowed

Rounds & Format:

  • Round 1 :
    • Problem statements along with the official presentation template will be released in the third week of February.
    • Teams must prepare and submit their idea proposals strictly using the provided template.
    • Proposals will be evaluated on innovation, technical approach, feasibility, scalability, novelty, and impact.
    • Last date for PPT submission: 21st March 2026.
    • The top 30 teams will be shortlisted for Round 2.
    • Shortlist announcement: 28th March 2026 (tentative).
  • Round 2 :
    • Round 2 will be conducted offline at the COEP Technological University campus in Pune on the 4th and 5th of April 2026.
    • Selected teams will develop a working prototype based on their submitted idea.
    • The hackathon will conclude with a final presentation and demo before the judges.
    • Meals and accommodation will be provided for the event duration. 

Prize Pool: ₹1 Lakh in Cash Prizes, Exclusive Goodies 

Problem Tracks: The Participants Can Choose Any One of The Following Tracks :

  • AI-Powered Translation Studio
    • Develop an intelligent translation platform that validates source quality, reuses past translations using RAG, enforces glossary and style rules, and continuously learns from approved corrections to improve translation consistency and efficiency.
  • US Healthcare EDI Parser & X12 File Validator (837 / 835 / 834)
    • Build a web application that parses, validates, and audits healthcare EDI files (claims, remittance, enrollment). The system should detect errors, provide plain-language explanations, suggest corrections, and include an AI assistant for contextual queries and summaries.
  • AI Email Coordination Assistant
    • Create an autonomous AI email assistant that reads availability emails, coordinates meeting schedules, creates Google Calendar events, and provides contextual thread updates — operating as a digital executive assistant.
  • AI-Powered Autonomous Drone Response for Urban Safety
    • Design a simulation-based urban safety system that detects incidents from video feeds, dispatches the nearest drone automatically, and visualizes real-time drone movement and alerts on a command dashboard.

For more details regarding the problem statements, please refer to the problem statements brief in the Download Attachments Section below. 

Rules for Round 1 Submission :

  • The submissions must be made in pdf format using the template given below. do not use any other template format for the submission
  • Teams must adhere to the given timeline.
  • Any Form of Plagiarism or Rule Violation Will Lead to Immediate Disqualification.

Evaluation Criteria: Innovation, Technical Implementation, Feasibility, Scalability, novelty, Impact

data.title: WCE Hackathon 2026
data.details:
WCE Hackathon 2026 marks the 10th Edition of the flagship hackathon organized by WCE ACM Student Chapter, celebrating a decade of innovation, collaboration, and problem-solving excellence.

WCE Hackathon 2026 will be conducted entirely in Offline mode for the implementation round. The first round will be conducted online, while the implementation round will be conducted offline. WCE Hackathon 2026 is a developing venture where participants are expected to complete product development as per the selected problem statements. In this hackathon, participants will innovate, strategize, code, and beat the odds with ingenious solutions to real-life problems. 

The Expert Track focuses on addressing Artificial Intelligence (AI) Systems through innovative solutions. Participants in this track will have the opportunity to create impactful solutions and may even secure internship opportunities with Zenteiq.

Hackathon Phases:

  • Official Announcement: February 2, 2026
  • Round 1 (Online): February 2, 2026 - February 25, 2026
  • Result Declaration of Round 1 (Expert Track): March 6, 2026
  • Result Declaration of Round 1 (Novice Track): March 8, 2025
  • Round 2 (Offline): March 20, 2026 - March 21, 2026
  • Result Declaration of Round 2: March 21, 2026

Tracks: The Hackathon will consist of 2 tracks i.e. Novice and Expert. The top 3 teams from both Expert track and the Novice track will be declared winners.

  • Novice Track: Teams of students from the 1st or 2nd year will be considered under this track. Themes for the Novice Track are provided in the guidelines document included in the zip file shared with participants.
  • Expert Track: Teams of students with at least one member from the 3rd or 4th year will compete in this track. The Expert Track includes problem statements related to Artificial Intelligence(AI) Systems created by Zenteiq.
  • Note: BCA Final Year Students will be considered in the Expert Track.

Note: Download the Brief/Case file attached in the Round 1 section to know the Presentation Format and also the Themes for both tracks. The file can be downloaded only after completing your registration.
